title: ALERTCalifornia's AI flags a 3 am smoke column near Mount Laguna; human operators verify it and Cal Fire holds the fire to under a quarter acre
summary: ALERTCalifornia's AI flagged smoke on a Cleveland National Forest camera at about 3 am on 5 August 2023, and Cal Fire held the verified fire under a quarter acre.
account: The ALERTCalifornia AI, a machine-learned model run by the University of California San Diego, watches live feeds from more than 1,000 cameras. Its watch over the feeds began at the end of June 2023 under a Cal Fire trial. At about 3 am on 5 August 2023, the AI flagged a column of smoke in the Cleveland National Forest near Mount Laguna. That is about 40 miles east of San Diego. Human operators verified the detection and alerted Cal Fire. The Los Angeles Times reported on 24 August 2023 that Cal Fire Battalion Chief Scott Slumpff got the confirmed alert just before 3 am and that crews held the fire to a 10-foot-by-10-foot spot. Slumpff said that without the alert nobody would have known about the fire until the next morning, and he judged that it would probably have reached hundreds of acres. On 12 September 2023 AFP reported that the operators had alerted Cal Fire Captain Kris Yeary and that his crews put the fire out at less than a quarter acre. Yeary told AFP that it could have become a devastating fire had the AI not alerted them. By September 2023 the tool reached all 21 Cal Fire dispatch centers. Cal Fire's figures for 2024 show that the cameras picked up 1,668 of 7,553 wildfires in its jurisdiction, 636 of them before any 911 call.
purpose: The tool was built to spot smoke in ALERTCalifornia camera feeds and notify Cal Fire emergency command centers. Crews can then reach a fire in its incipient phase. This detection was that purpose.
system: ALERTCalifornia AI wildfire detection (machine-learned smoke and anomaly detection on the ALERTCalifornia pan-tilt-zoom camera network)
developer: ALERTCalifornia, University of California San Diego, with industry partner Digital Path
deployer: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE)
segment: State fire agency using a university camera network

ratings.reason: Cal Fire's Mount Laguna station received a verified alert at about 3 am. Its crews extinguished the fire at under a quarter acre. Cal Fire intelligence specialist Suzann Leininger said: “It's getting us time to react in a faster manner”.

The area around Mount Laguna was spared a larger fire. Captain Yeary judged that it “could have been a devastating fire”. Battalion Chief Slumpff judged that it would probably have reached hundreds of acres. No source measures what would have happened without the alert.

ai_role.statement: The model's contribution was the detection. Its algorithm flagged a smoke column in a Cleveland National Forest camera feed at about 3 am. Human operators verified it before Cal Fire was alerted. The containment was done by Captain Yeary's crews. No source records whether a 911 call would have come later. The time gained is documented only for the program as a whole. TIME reports 77 fires identified before any 911 call in the first two months. UC San Diego's Neal Driscoll says the alerts beat 911 calls about 40 percent of the time. AFP also notes the system sometimes misreads dust, insects or weather as smoke. That is why the human verification step sits between the model and the dispatch.

The Los Angeles Times reported separately from interviews with Cal Fire staff and the ALERTCalifornia director. The Bay Area News Group report gives Cal Fire's figures for 2024. fields.summary: ALERTCalifornia's AI flagged smoke on a Cleveland National Forest camera at about 3 am on 5 August 2023, and Cal Fire held the verified fire under a quarter acre.
fields.account: The ALERTCalifornia AI, a machine-learned model run by the University of California San Diego, watches live feeds from more than 1,000 cameras. Its watch over the feeds began at the end of June 2023 under a Cal Fire trial. At about 3 am on 5 August 2023, the AI flagged a column of smoke in the Cleveland National Forest near Mount Laguna. That is about 40 miles east of San Diego. Human operators verified the detection and alerted Cal Fire. The Los Angeles Times reported on 24 August 2023 that Cal Fire Battalion Chief Scott Slumpff got the confirmed alert just before 3 am and that crews held the fire to a 10-foot-by-10-foot spot. Slumpff said that without the alert nobody would have known about the fire until the next morning, and he judged that it would probably have reached hundreds of acres. On 12 September 2023 AFP reported that the operators had alerted Cal Fire Captain Kris Yeary and that his crews put the fire out at less than a quarter acre. Yeary told AFP that it could have become a devastating fire had the AI not alerted them. By September 2023 the tool reached all 21 Cal Fire dispatch centers. Cal Fire's figures for 2024 show that the cameras picked up 1,668 of 7,553 wildfires in its jurisdiction, 636 of them before any 911 call.
